title: Retain incomplete transcript records until the next append
evidence: readlines() consumes an unterminated trailing record, last_pos=f.tell() advances past it, and extract_model_change silently drops JSON decode failures.
trigger: A writer appends a JSON record in two writes straddling a watcher polling interval.
impact: The first fragment is discarded and the remaining fragment cannot reconstruct the record, permanently losing the model-change announcement.

title: Reset tail position when transcript is truncated or replaced
evidence: Only curr_size > last_pos is handled; last_pos is never reset and no file identity is tracked.
trigger: The watched transcript is truncated/rotated and the replacement starts shorter than the prior offset.
impact: Announcements stop until the new file exceeds the old size and then resume from an arbitrary offset, losing earlier replacement-file events.

title: Pass notification text as data rather than AppleScript source
evidence: The cached-audio branch interpolates text directly into osascript -e source inside a quoted string; subprocess receives this source unchanged.
trigger: speak_cloned receives quote-bearing text and the corresponding cached/direct WAV exists (lines 51-58).
impact: Text can terminate the AppleScript string, corrupt the notification or introduce AppleScript expressions under the announcer account. The cache-hit precondition limits reachability; no remote trust boundary is asserted.

title: Validate envelope length before slicing the shared-memory payload
evidence: env.data[..env.len] precedes unpack validation. IpcEnvelope has public len: usize and data: [u8; 8192] (bft_iceoryx2.rs:78-81); bindings.rs:211-214 exposes this writer through start_writer_daemon.
trigger: An IPC publisher submits an IpcEnvelope with len > 8192.
impact: The writer thread panics before rejecting malformed input, stopping ingestion until restarted. No claim of memory unsafety is made.

title: Reject invalid payload hash text instead of signing a zero digest
evidence: payload_hash starts as [0;32]; decoding only runs for length 64 and successful hex decode, but BftMessage::sign is unconditional at line 111. bindings.rs:203-205 forwards arbitrary Python hash strings.
trigger: publish_node is called with a malformed or wrong-length hexadecimal digest.
impact: The call returns success and publishes a valid signature over a different all-zero digest, silently losing payload identity.

title: CTRE commits non-finite drift observations
evidence: No finiteness validation before percentile/mean; NaN propagates as var_limit when tail_risks is empty (31-39), and NaN > threshold is false at line 52.
trigger: Call enforce_thermodynamic_brake with a NaN-containing list, including [float("nan")].
impact: Returns ACTION_COMMIT and records a non-finite risk rather than rejecting invalid observations. Traced consumer eip7702_hunter.py:65-73 only updates counters/messages; no actual on-chain execution is established.

title: Risk rounding precedes CTRE threshold enforcement
evidence: cvar_risk is rounded to five decimals at line 50 before strict threshold comparison at line 52.
trigger: Default threshold 0.015 and an observation such as 0.015004, whose CVaR exceeds the threshold but rounds to 0.015.
impact: Reports ACTION_COMMIT despite exceeding the configured maximum risk. Observed consumer is a simulator/counter, not proven transaction execution.

title: Proposal handler fabricates verified postconditions without independent execution
evidence: process_request routes public tools/call and skills.propose_effect to handle_skills_propose_effect (1987-1998). The handler unconditionally returns status VERIFIED and postconditions_checked with broker_state Authorized and effects_executed 0 (1888-1898). Its optional verifier also takes both observed_post_hash and actual_file_sha256 from the same request, defaulting the latter to the former (1831-1856).
trigger: Submit an otherwise admissible proposal without simulated_execution_result; or supply matching fabricated postcondition hashes in that request.
impact: The MCP response reports completed independent verification for an unexecuted proposal; caller-supplied simulation data can additionally advance broker verification state. This is an evidence/state integrity defect; no unauthorized physical execution is demonstrated.

title: Legacy read methods bypass configured project visibility
evidence: is_skill_visible applies project_allowlists (1242-1252), and discover/inspect/propose call it. process_request handles skills/get, resources/read, prompts/list and prompts/get directly against snapshot maps (2050-2187), without a project identity or visibility check.
trigger: Configure a project allowlist excluding a loaded skill, then request its known skill:// URI using resources/read or its prompt using prompts/get.
impact: The caller can load the excluded skill instructions/resources despite the configured visibility filter. This exposes snapshot content; it does not itself confer effect execution authority.

title: Cache audit resolves benchmark below scripts instead of repository root
evidence: Two dirname calls on scripts/c5_quality_gates/run_cache_audit.py produce scripts/. Lines 26-27 then select scripts/tests/cache_kinetic_benchmark.cpp; targeted file inventory locates source at tests/cache_kinetic_benchmark.cpp.
trigger: Run the documented cache audit runner from the repository.
impact: Compilation receives a nonexistent source path and the audit exits before collecting benchmark evidence.

title: Cache report unconditionally claims mitigation and patentability
evidence: The runner writes a fixed conclusion asserting complete L1 false-sharing mitigation and technical patentability after any exit-zero benchmark. It neither parses measurements nor checks a threshold or environment.
trigger: After fixing the path issue, benchmark exits zero even when results do not show the expected performance improvement.
impact: Generated evidence states success independent of measured results and makes a patentability assertion unsupported by the benchmark.

title: Purge unlinks live SQLite WAL and shared-memory files
evidence: Lines 178–190 classify every *.db-wal/*.db-shm as orphan and unlink it, without opening/checkpointing the database, checking live users, or applying CANONICAL_PROTECTED_DIRS.
trigger: Invoke bundled script without --dry-run on a workspace containing a WAL-mode database with uncheckpointed committed writes.
impact: Deletes recovery data and coordination files; subsequent database access can lose committed changes or encounter corruption. This is a callable bundled maintenance script, not evidence that it has been executed.

title: Workspace purge resets unrelated live global sessions
evidence: Lines 193–207 unconditionally target ~/.gemini/antigravity/conversation_summaries.db and UPDATE every RUNNING/not_fully_idle row to IDLE. No workspace filter or process-liveness check exists.
trigger: Run purge for any workspace while another Antigravity conversation is running.
impact: Global session bookkeeping is changed to idle despite live work, outside the selected workspace and without establishing that listeners are ghosts.

title: Bounded advisory queues silently discard accepted frames
evidence: All domain queues use deque(maxlen=capacity); _route_advisory appends without checking fullness and dispatch_frame increments total_dispatched. bounty_pipeline_orchestrator.py:109–116 dispatches the entire batch before draining.
trigger: More than queue_capacity valid advisories for one domain arrive in a cycle before drainage.
impact: Oldest accepted advisories disappear without rejection or loss telemetry; specialist processing misses them.

title: Rekor public key contract disagrees with both ledger callers
evidence: anchor_payload documents public_key_pem and base64-encodes its UTF-8 contents into publicKey.content. ledger_actor.py lines 341–352 and cortex_persist_ledger.py lines 804–815 instead pass base64 of the raw 32-byte NaCl verification key. Thus the submitted key decodes to base64 text rather than the promised PEM public key.
trigger: Either ledger uses the default RekorClient to anchor its head.
impact: The callers do not satisfy the client key encoding contract; anchoring requests contain an incorrectly serialized public key. Remote acceptance was not tested.

title: Symmetry verifier ignores additional reverse-kernel mass
evidence: Only (x,y) pairs present in F are checked. For p={a:1}, F={a:{y:1}}, D={y:{a:1,b:1}}, all inspected terms match although the reverse joint has extra mass at b.
trigger: Pass a supplied D with extra support not represented by F.
impact: verify_symmetry returns true for unequal joint distributions, weakening the exported mathematical validation routine.

title: Inbound email acknowledges exhausted webhook delivery failures
evidence: After three failed fetch attempts, the handler only logs and resolves; no rejection, throw, forwarding or durable queue exists in this handler.
trigger: Webhook rejects or remains unavailable for all three attempts.
impact: Email handler reports completion while email payload has not been delivered or durably retained.

title: Technical specification recommends weaker persistence than the canonical contract
evidence: Connection configuration uses PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL; .babylon60rules requires synchronous = FULL and ledger.rs:57 implements FULL.
trigger: An implementer copies section 3.1 as the connection configuration for a new persistent ledger.
impact: The normative example contradicts the required durability setting and can propagate a weaker persistence configuration.

title: Stress example certifies latency bounds without checking them
evidence: Baseline <5ns success at 100 is unconditional; poison timer starts only after poison_thread.join (285-291); <1ms certification at 298 has no latency assertion; final sub-100ns text at 309 is fixed.
trigger: Run example on hardware or scheduling conditions that exceed the printed latency thresholds.
impact: Example still prints certified bounds; poison timing omits the interval between poisoning and producer join, so it cannot substantiate propagation latency.

title: Compliance pipeline verifies a different artifact than the certificate it generated
evidence: Generated signed_cert is written to official_eu_compliance_certificate.json at lines 87-89, but verifier receives eu_ai_act_annex_vi_pack.json at lines 102-104; no linkage or status check precedes the unconditional 100% Conforme verdict at line 113. Exporter verify_evidence uses UNVERIFIED_NO_LEDGER when no ledger is supplied.
trigger: Run the demo with a pre-existing pack that satisfies the verifier while the newly generated certificate has unverified evidence.
impact: Successful verification of the separate pack is misreported as validation of the newly generated evidence chain.

title: Benchmark extrapolates Python loops into isolation guarantees
evidence: Both branches compute the same SHA-256 predicate; the eBPF branch additionally runs empty Python loops. No eBPF, syscall, shared-memory IPC, isolation, or agent termination is exercised. A measured speedup prints that a corrupt agent dies at zero cost.
trigger: Run stress_test and obtain speedup > 2.
impact: The printed success certifies unsupported isolation and zero-cost claims from an intentionally unequal simulation.

title: Limit terminology rewrites to comments and documentation
evidence: For any MythologicalTerm issue the fixer applies every replacement regex to the entire file, including executable identifiers, protocol strings and literals.
trigger: A flagged source file contains an identifier or protocol value named oracle or magic referenced elsewhere.
impact: Running the fixer changes code behavior or breaks cross-file references without updating consumers; terminology cleanup is not semantics preserving.

title: Report labels a byte-count formula as dissipated energy
evidence: Lines 246–247 calculate total_bits * LANDAUER_BOUND_300K; line 386 prints Landauer disipado. No energy measurement or count of erased bits enters the formula.
trigger: Run the synthetic workload and consume the final energy report.
impact: A theoretical constant multiplied by input size is presented as measured dissipation, making the energy evidence misleading.

title: Oncology support check cannot detect an out-of-support target
evidence: implied_targets is built exclusively from targets; prior_supp contains all IDs in targets; implied_targets - prior_supp is therefore always empty (lines 74-84).
trigger: A drug record mentions an unknown target not represented in the ontology.
impact: A4 still reports PASS and contributes to ONTOLOGY SOUND without checking the missing target.

title: Frame event ID and payload separately in Merkle commitments
evidence: new() hashes event_id.as_bytes(), then payload, then parent_hash without lengths or separators; constructor accepts arbitrary String IDs.
trigger: Construct nodes with the same parent and (event_id="a",payload=b"bc") versus (event_id="ab",payload=b"c").
impact: Both distinct nodes receive the same state_hash without breaking SHA-256. The exported constructor does not bind field boundaries; current in-file tests use fixed-form IDs only.

title: Tenant example treats a lower bound as prefix isolation
evidence: The Multitenancy example has only folder gte tenants/${tenantId}/ and calls it a starts-with pattern. Official Cloudflare filtering documentation defines gte as greater-than-or-equal and requires an upper bound for folder prefix matching: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/retrieval/filtering/ ; legacy format documentation also requires two range bounds: https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/api/migration/autorag-filter-format/ .
trigger: A developer adapts the multitenancy example to an API accepting its filter shape in an index shared across tenants.
impact: A lexically later tenant folder satisfies the lone lower bound; this example is insufficient to isolate tenant retrieval. Current APIs may reject this older filter shape instead. No active deployed consumer was established.

title: Swing formula does not implement its declared triplet ratio
evidence: At swing_pct=66.7 the code computes int((16.7/50)*(120*0.667))=26 ticks; a 240-tick sixteenth pair at 66.7 percent places the second note near tick 160, requiring about 40 ticks offset.
trigger: Choose 66.7 percent swing (the source explicitly calls this pure triplet swing).
impact: Generated offbeat timing is about 146 rather than 160 ticks, so the supplied swing percentage and stated triplet behavior disagree.

title: Comment stripping corrupts quoted URLs in tsconfig
evidence: JSONC_COMMENT_RE matches // through the end of a line without tracking strings. _load_jsonc applies it before json.loads and suppresses parsing failures as {}. ts_aliases then loses compilerOptions.paths; extract_js classifies unresolved alias imports as external registry candidates.
trigger: A valid tsconfig contains a quoted URL such as a $schema URL and path aliases.
impact: The scanner silently discards valid configuration and may flag working alias imports as phantom external packages.

title: Draft filenames accept path components from campaign JSON
evidence: lead_id is interpolated directly into output_drafts_dir / filename and write_text; no basename or containment validation.
trigger: An audited/passable campaign lead has an absolute lead_id or ../ segments and --save-drafts is used.
impact: Draft can overwrite a writable text path outside the requested drafts directory; parent directory must exist.
